item.title: After Trump promised to pay $5,000 if Republicans win, here's what to expect Thursday
item.description: President Trump promised to send every adult citizen $5,000, but only if Republicans maintain control of Congress in the midterm election, setting high expectations for the convention's final night.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: NPR's Michel Martin asks Maine's Democratic Governor Janet Mills about the impact of the escalating U.S.-Canada trade war on her state.

item.title: Trump officials revive a bid to alter the U.S. census and reshape voting maps
item.description: The Trump administration is making a new push to exclude millions of U.S. residents from a key census count that the 14th Amendment says must include the "whole number of persons in each state."

item.title: 1 year later, young conservatives still grapple with Charlie Kirk's death
item.description: One year later, Charlie Kirk's death continues to resonate deeply with young conservatives across the country -- including many on the campus of Utah Valley University where he was killed.

item.title: A pilot of the Amazon cargo plane in Miami crash warned it was coming in too fast
item.description: For nearly two minutes, one of the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane that careened off a Miami runway repeatedly warned his counterpart they were going too fast, according to flight information.

item.title: Investigators release information from flight data recorder in Miami plane crash
item.description: Safety investigators are releasing new details about the moments before the deadly cargo plane crash in Miami on Sunday, raising questions about the actions of the two pilots.

item.title: Conductor Julian Wachner receives suspended sentence for possession of child sex abuse material
item.description: The formerly prominent, widely recorded conductor was sentenced Wednesday to nearly six years of probation for five counts of possession of child sex abuse material in Indianapolis.

item.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns
item.description: The leader of the Education Department's special education office told employees she is resigning after less than four months in the role and as the agency overall is morphing and shrinking.

item.title: Andrew Tate is denied bail and will remain in jail during his extradition fight
item.description: Prosecutors told the court that Andrew and Tristan Tate boasted about having multiple passports and flying on private jets. But the Tates' lawyers argued they were only playing a role for their fans.
